| 2 b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Coconut (02 -35 years above): Kerala root wilt in Tamil Nadu. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7. rows: a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 05th June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important
reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 56.80 Billion Cubic Meter, which is
31.1% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 138
percent of last year's storage and 129 percent of the average storage of the last ten years
during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the
corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the
Normal storage during the corresponding period.

chunks.text: Period Average (LPA) by 106%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th Mar to 31st May, 2025) is higher than LPA by 42%. Rainfall Forecast: - Overall rainfall activity is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of central India and below normal over northwest, east & northeast India during the week Advance of Southwest Monsoon: - The Northern Limit of Monsoon continues to pass through 17.0°N/55°E, 17.5°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18.5°N/70°E, Mumbai, Ahilyanagar, Adilabad, Bhawanipatna, Puri, Sandhead Island, 23.5°N/89.5°E, Balurghat, 30°N/85°E. | 4 - Southwest Monsoon likely to advance over some more parts of Central & east India during week 2 (12 to 18 June, 2025). | 5 Temerature Week 1 (06th – 11th June 2025): - Maximum Temperatures likely to rise by 2-3°C over Northwest & Central India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. - No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. Week 2 ( 12th – 18th June 2025): - Maximum temperatures are likely to increase over northwest India as compared to week1.

chunks.heading: 3. RESERVOIR STORAGE (as on 05th June, 2025)
chunks.text:
Current live storage in 161 reservoirs was 56.80 BCM (31.1%) of total live capacity of 182.44 BCM. Table 1: For 161 major reservoirs of the country - 128 reservoirs having storage more than 80% of normal storage. - 21 reservoirs having storage 51% to 80%. - 12 reservoirs having storage upto 50%.
